decisive_items: Gradual hair loss of the eyelashes, eyebrows, beard, and scalp for 4 years
Diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis (hematoxylin-eosin stain)
response.rationale: The combination of chronic madarosis, diffuse facial infiltration, joint involvement, uveitis, lymphadenopathy, and foamy histiocyte infiltrate with numerous acid-fast bacilli is classic for lepromatous leprosy. The acid-fast bacilli are pathognomonic and outweigh the non-specific joint/RF findings. Lupus vulgaris also has acid-fast bacilli but typically presents with plaques and lacks the systemic pattern seen here.

rejected.why: Lupus pernio is a sarcoidosis variant; no acid-fast bacilli and the clinical pattern (madarosis, diffuse infiltration) is not typical.
Sarcoidosis can cause uveitis, lymphadenopathy, and skin nodules, but the presence of acid-fast bacilli and foamy histiocytes with madarosis strongly favors leprosy.
Lupus vulgaris is a cutaneous tuberculosis with acid-fast bacilli, but the diffuse facial infiltration, madarosis, and systemic features (uveitis, splenomegaly) are more characteristic of leprosy.
Rheumatoid arthritis explains joint symptoms and elevated RF, but the skin biopsy with acid-fast bacilli and the pattern of hair loss are not compatible.
